title: How a Computer Boots: Firmware, Bootloader, Kernel and init
oneLiner: From the power button to a login prompt: UEFI and BIOS, POST, the EFI System Partition, Secure Boot, GRUB, the kernel and initramfs, and systemd as PID 1, with where each boot failure comes from.
keyTakeaway: Booting is a chain: firmware runs POST and finds a bootloader, the bootloader loads the kernel and initramfs, the kernel mounts the root filesystem and starts PID 1, which starts everything else. Secure Boot checks a signature at each step. Match the error message to the stage to know where to look.
explanation:
Every boot follows the same chain of programs, each loading the next. Step through it on a modern UEFI machine running Linux, with the Windows equivalents, then compare legacy BIOS and MBR with UEFI and GPT.

The lesson ends with a table that matches common boot failures, from "no bootable device" to a kernel panic, to the stage that failed and what to check first.
